headline: 1%: Public Record Shows All 500 Approved PAC-3 MSE Interceptors Operational in Ukraine by 1 December
deck: The U.S. approved the purchase and allied financing; there is a 1% chance that a qualifying public record establishes all 500 are operational in Ukraine by 1 December.
body: The U.S. Department of State approved a possible $2.1 billion sale of 500 PAC-3 MSE missiles for Ukraine’s Patriot air-defence systems. AP reported that Kyiv had accused the Pentagon of delaying delivery of the munition needed against ballistic missiles. [E1][E5]

Ukraine’s request includes the interceptors, spare parts, related equipment, and logistical and software support. Canada, Germany and Norway are to contribute through JUMPSTART, alongside national funds raised through the European Union’s Ukraine Support Loan. [E2][E3]

Ukrinform reported that deliveries may begin only in a few years. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the authorization strong. RBC Ukraine reported that the 500 missiles could provide protection as early as this winter but that deliveries would not begin for several years; Al Jazeera reported that two people briefed on the U.S. decision expected delivery a couple of years into the 2030s. [E4][E6][E7][E8]

On August 2, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Patriot systems had no interceptors ready during a Kyiv attack. This approval is a new purchase authorization, with no published delivery timetable. [E9][E4]

**The desk's reading.** There is a 1% probability that a qualifying public record will establish that all 500 approved PAC-3 MSE interceptors are delivered to Ukraine and operationally available by 1 December 2026; that is the question the forecast label settles. Separately, the probability that all 500 will actually be operationally available by that date is also 1%. The reported multi-year delivery timetable puts both estimates near zero; the approval and financing move the availability estimate to 1%, but neither supplies a winter delivery schedule. The strongest competing reading is that partners could transfer existing stocks while the order is fulfilled, but the published record here provides no such transfer or delivery schedule. [E1][E3][E4][E7][E8]

**The next test.** This forecast settles YES only if the U.S. government, the Ukrainian government, or a supplier publishes a record by 1 December 2026 that the interceptors have been delivered to Ukraine and made operationally available; it settles NO if no such record appears by that deadline. A documented inventory transfer and Ukrainian operational confirmation would overturn the reading; their absence keeps the production clock ahead of the winter claim.
